hypothesis: Validate endpoint control characters only on first insertion into the per-call aggregation map. Existing keys necessarily passed the same char::is_control predicate, and exact str equality certifies subsequent occurrences without rescanning their characters. This enables the standard split_once TAB search instead of a scalar endpoint scan on every record. Round-2 development evidence leaves Unicode-endpoint cases at roughly 92-105 ns per record versus about 60-76 ns for low-cardinality ASCII cases; repeated Unicode decoding and per-record endpoint scanning are a concrete remaining cost, although this is not profiling evidence. The change can also benefit repeated ASCII endpoints while leaving numeric parsing, randomized hashing and final sorting unchanged.
notes: Fresh model-authored proposal based on round-2-preselection exported development evidence. No local compile, test or benchmark was run. This is a single endpoint-validation-hoisting change, not a workload-size heuristic: the existing HashMap itself proves which exact endpoints are valid. Invalid endpoints are never inserted, and invalid row counts remain per occurrence. There is no global or cross-call cache or extra validation cache. Full char::is_control semantics remain authoritative for both ASCII and Unicode on first insertion; starts_with slash is checked on every row. Numeric overflow, signs, leading zeroes, field count and line-ending behavior remain unchanged. Risks: mostly-unique endpoints reduce validation reuse, and rows with valid numbers but invalid endpoint controls now perform a hash lookup before rejection, which may regress heavily malformed input. Standard hasher seed variability remains. The anticipated incremental gain is credible but unmeasured and must exceed the controller threshold.
